turns: Which hubs in the Midwest are most exposed to winter disruption?
results.answer: Minneapolis (MSP) is the Midwest hub most exposed to winter disruption, with a winter score of 48.2. Chicago (CHI) is next at 39.9 and Detroit (DTW) is third at 37.4. All three are only 'moderate' in absolute terms, so none is 'high'. MSP has 146.4 freeze days/yr (min temp <= 0 C) and 20.4 days/yr with snowfall >= 1 cm. CHI has 103.6 freeze days and 18.6 snow days. DTW has 111.4 freeze days and 17.0 snow days. Kansas City (MCI) scores 33.8, which is moderate. Indianapolis (IND, 30.7) and Columbus (CMH, 30.1) are low. CHI and DTW are not a close call (2.5 points apart is not flagged), but CHI is flagged as a close call with the next hub. The text above only supports the flag as given, and the flag is on CHI vs DTW per the tool output. IND and CMH are also a close call, so their order is not meaningful.

turns: Compare Miami and Houston in terms of hurricane and flood exposure.
results.answer: Miami has the higher hurricane/wind exposure, and Houston has much higher flood exposure. Wind: Miami scores 51.9 (moderate) and Houston 43.1 (moderate). The gap comes mainly from FEMA wind declarations, 11 for Miami and 8 for Houston over 20 years. Gust days are similar: 11.8 days/yr at or above 60 km/h for Miami and 10.8 for Houston. Flood: Houston scores 74.7 (high) and Miami 32.4 (low). Houston has 23.6 days/yr with at least 25 mm of rain and 4.2 days/yr with at least 50 mm. Miami has 9.2 and 2.2 days/yr. Houston also has 7 FEMA flood declarations against 2 for Miami. Houston's composite is 39.0 and Miami's is 22.7, both moderate and low respectively. Neither hub's wind score is high in absolute terms.
